content:
alex: Heads up — saw a regression after the infra driver bump on the ci-gpu pool. ~20% tail latency increase on seqlen=512 generation jobs. Traces point to unexpected kernel path selection + KV cache churn.

maya: which driver bump? and which kernel path is being chosen? :thinking:

alex: driver moved from 525.x -> 535.x on the pool. Runtime is picking an FP8/tensor-core fastpath for some cards where tensor core FP8 ops then fallback during runtime init, causing a lot of small fallbacks and cold KV cache misses.

simon: can you paste the probe output from the failing host?

alex: sure — snippet from the device capability probe on one repro node:

```
cap_probe: pci=0000:3b:00.0 name=Turing-like-X
cap_probe: sm=86 reported_tensor_cores=1
cap_probe: queried_hw_fp8=1
cap_probe: try_init_fp8_kernels -> kernel_alloc: failed (OOM-like) -> fallback to bf16_gemm
cap_probe: effective_fp8_path=disabled (post-init)
```

alex: note the probe initially records fp8 as available but the runtime later falls back during kernel instantiation. That mismatch results in selecting the fast FP8 kernel path in the dispatcher, then hitting the slower fallback per-inference which thrashes the KV cache and batching heuristics.

julia: this smells like two independent issues: (1) driver/OS reporting capability bits too optimistically, (2) our selection logic not re-evaluating after kernel init failure. We should short-circuit selection on any init failure.

maya: agree. Also worth noting: the repro traces show increased host<->device memcpy counts around the same time — consistent with KV cache invalidation and re-uploads when fallback flips mid-request.

tao: I pushed a tiny profiler capture to the job linked by eng-bot: https://eng-bot/profiles/1715009999/pprof. Key line from pprof flame: FP8_gemm_init -> fallback_handler -> kv_upload_hotpath.

ryan: for mitigation, we should add a capability override env var and a defensive re-probe on kernel init failure. e.g. in config: `capability_overrides: { "force_no_fp8": true }` and a flag `reprobe_on_init_failure=true`. That would avoid the mid-flight flips.

simon: +1. Also add a diagnostic metric: `kernel_init_status{model,host,capability}="failed"` so we can alert when init failures happen post-probe.

julia: minor patch idea: when a selected kernel reports init failure, mark that kernel family as disabled for that device for at least N seconds, and switch dispatcher to compatible fallback without reselecting per-request. Avoids thrash.

alex: test notes: repro only happens under high concurrency (batching enabled + KV cache warm) and when memory fragmentation is high (long-running node). Fresh node without fragmentation doesn't repro. So CI test needs to simulate fragmentation.

maya: can we add a small reproducer script for infra to run? e.g. allocate several persistent large tensors first, then run a short FP8 microbench to trigger init path.

```
# repro sketch (not final):
python repro/mem_frag_repro.py --reserve-gb 12 --run-microbench fp8_init
```

ryan: I'll open a PR to add `force_no_fp8` override + the init-failure-disable TTL. Also will wire the metric.

eng-bot: created issue #INF-4291 "defensive kernel init & capability reprobe" and linked PR draft https://eng-bot/pr/4921

alex: action items we agreed on:
- ryan: PR for override + disable-on-init-failure (urgent)
- simon: add kernel_init_status metric + dashboard panel
- maya: repro script and CI job to simulate fragmentation
- julia/tao: add dispatcher guard to avoid per-request reselection on init flip and a TTL for disabled kernels

maya: one more ask — capture exact driver package & CUDA runtime on the repro nodes and add to the issue. Could be driver/CUDA coupling.

alex: noted. I'll attach logs & driver info to INF-4291. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
